items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Freeman opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Freeman provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: Urban Heat Island Mapping
notes: Peter J. Crank, Ph.D., Assistant Professor of Geography & Environmental Management, University of Waterloo and Gagandeep Singh, Graduate Research Assistant, University of Waterloo gave a presentation on the effects of urban heat islands, with a list of recommendations to mitigate them. They then responded to questions of Council.

That consent motion items (a) through (d) be approved.

2024 Generally Recruited Representative

items.title: Uptown Community Improvement Plan
notes: Kristin Sainsbury responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Waterloo Park – Eby Farmstead Animals
notes: Robin Milne offered some introductory remarks to the report.
Diego Almaraz, Resident of Waterloo gave a presentation asking Council to consider using the Eby Farmstead area as a temporary off-leash dog park while the Waterloo Park Planning is underway.
Robin Milne and Anna lee Sangster then responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Questions
notes: Councillor Wright asked staff about a potential vacant buildings policy, as the City does not currently have one. She requested an update on it and the timeline. Ron Ormson responded stating that the policy would be a joint effort between Building Standards and Municipal Enforcement. He went over some of the risks of leaving vacant buildings and mentioned that while the conversation had been on pause due to staff workloads, it should be reactivated again in early Q1 next year.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Vasic had a chance to go to the Child and Youth Planning Table Conference at the Kitchener Public Library the previous week, November 14-15. The topic was, “Forward Together: Activating Change, Amplifying Belonging.” There were great speakers, local and otherwise, speaking about youth belonging in the City and youth engagement. She’s been thinking about what activates belonging, how overlooked youth are, especially those who don’t play sports in facilities, and how we oversee certain equity-denied groups. She offered thanks to the Child and Youth Planning Table and staff that were in attendance, including most of the READI team and some of the Neighbourhoods team.

Councillor Roach mentioned that this coming Saturday, November 23, the Lakeshore South Community was hosting a free skate at Albert McCormick at 2:00pm. He reflected on a friend whose uncle would have turned 100 this month, Father David Bauer, a famous Waterloo resident who helped establish the men’s hockey national team.

Councillor Wright wanted to highlight that the Urban Canopy Tree Consultation was held on November 19, at 7:30pm, at the Community Pavilion in the Waterloo Memorial Recreation Complex. It is organized by Uptown West and brings residents who want to be able to provide feedback on the City’s engagement on tree canopy. She also shared that the Powering the Energy Transition event on the High Performance Development Standards was taking place at the Walper Hotel in Downtown Kitchener on Thursday, November 21 from 3:30-5:30pm.
